questions.stem: In a group of 50 people: 30 like cricket, 25 like football, and 10 like both. How many like neither?
Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship: India, Maharashtra, Mumbai?

options.option_text: Three concentric circles (Mumbai innermost, Maharashtra middle, India outermost)
Two separate circles inside a bigger circle

questions.explanation: A is correct. Mumbai ⊂ Maharashtra ⊂ India — each is fully contained within the next. Three concentric circles (nested) represent this perfectly.

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram best represents: Triangles, Quadrilaterals, Polygons?

options.option_text: Two overlapping circles inside a bigger circle
Two separate non-overlapping circles both inside a bigger circle

questions.explanation: C is correct. Triangles ⊂ Polygons and Quadrilaterals ⊂ Polygons, but Triangles and Quadrilaterals are mutually exclusive (no figure is both). So: two separate circles inside a larger Polygons circle.

questions.stem: In a class of 40 students: 25 play cricket, 20 play football, 15 play both. How many play only cricket?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Only cricket = total cricket − both = 25−15 = 10.

questions.stem: In a class of 60: 35 like Math, 45 like Science. All students like at least one subject. How many like both?
questions.explanation: B is correct. |M∪S| = total = 60 (everyone likes at least one). |M∪S| = |M|+|S|−|M∩S| → 60 = 35+45−|M∩S| → |M∩S| = 20.

questions.stem: Circle A has 12 elements, Circle B has 15 elements, and their intersection has 5 elements. What is |A∪B|?
In a group of 60 people: 35 like tea, 40 like coffee, 25 like both. How many like neither?
In a survey of 60 people who like Math, Science or English: 35 like Math, 40 like Science. If 15 like all three and 20 like exactly two, how many like only one subject?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total = only-one + exactly-two + all-three → 60 = only-one + 20 + 15 → only-one = 25.

questions.stem: 100 students: 60 like History, 55 like Geography, 50 like Civics. 30 like History & Geography, 25 like History & Civics, 20 like Geography & Civics, 10 like all three. How many like exactly two subjects?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Exactly two (excluding those who like all three): (H∩G only)=30−10=20, (H∩C only)=25−10=15, (G∩C only)=20−10=10. Total exactly two = 20+15+10 = 45.

questions.stem: From the same survey (100 students, Q9 data), how many like at least one of the three subjects?
questions.explanation: C is correct. |H∪G∪C| = 60+55+50−30−25−20+10 = 165−75+10 = 100. All 100 students like at least one subject — nobody likes none.
